_about: Ascot's main stand, assembled from the modules in assets/models/architecture/stand_modules.json. Order runs LEFT to RIGHT as seen from the track, which at Ascot is EAST (upstream) to WEST (past the post). 'repeat' places the same module that many times in a row. The stand is anchored so the clock tower faces the winning post; its front line is 'setback' metres behind the near (outer) rail of the home straight. Change the list and re-run tools/course/build_ascot_layout.py; the Blender build reads the same list. Since 6 Nov 2026 the long runs are the terrace stand from the owner's archive photos (the earlier order is kept as _previousOrder); an item's own 'bays' overrides the catalogue width (owner: no slivers; stair halls 2 bays, short terrace stretches at least 5, pavilions slimmed to pay for it). Owner's elevation markup (6 Nov 2026): the centrepiece is a 6-bay gallery block, the 8-bay iron lace bay with the tower in its centre, and a 6-bay gallery block; the west grand roof runs on over the iron bay and the last terrace.

groundTerraces._about: Owner, 9 Nov 2026: the stand moved back 6 m (setback 15.4 -> 21.4) and standing terraces stepping down to the lawn in front of the traditional pieces only (items with groundTerrace: the clock tower centre, and each iron lace bay with its grand canopy). rows x tread metres deep (7.6 m), each row rise higher, people on every row.
